title: How Iman Gadzhi closed $80K of SMMA retainers in 72 hours using anchoring, minimum terms and guarantees
summary: Iman walks through four agency deals closed in one weekend. He explains how he anchors price, trades lower retainers for longer minimums to raise guaranteed value, and separates logistics questions from objections. He also covers collecting payment on the call and his guarantee.

principles.text: Set a price anchor before you quote: have the prospect guess your rate so a lower offer feels like a steal.
principles.quote: I wanted to set that benchmark because then once I told him, okay, look, we're going to charge you £2,500 a month with a 6-month minimum, it seems like a total steal.

principles.text: Longer minimum terms can matter more than a higher monthly fee, so judge deals by guaranteed value and lower churn.
principles.quote: I'm starting to think more in terms of like the guaranteed value of the client.

principles.text: Tell logistics questions apart from objections: logistics means the buyer is sold and needs the delivery explained.
principles.quote: Objection handling is, you know, they're not sold on it, so they're trying to test. Whereas logistics handling is they're sold on it, but they just need to wrap their head around the logistics

principles.text: Don't leave the call until payment is taken; no payment means no client.
principles.quote: I am not leaving that call until payment.

principles.text: Extra calls add friction and lose deals, so close in as few calls as possible.
principles.quote: Any sort of added friction really ruins the likeliness of the sale.

principles.text: Offer a guarantee and take on the risk yourself. It removes the buyer's downside and forces you to pick clients carefully.
principles.quote: we guarantee a return on ad spend. Um, so that's 1.5x. So that basically means it's physically impossible for you to lose money.
